title: Grand-jury recommendations promised and still not done
question: Which Civil Grand Jury recommendations did a department say it would carry out, and still report as not done?
finding: Across 16 grand-jury reports from the 2021-22 to 2024-25 juries, 77 department responses promised to carry out a recommendation at some point. 31 of them were still reported as 'will be implemented in the future' or 'requires further analysis' at the latest report, 15 of them from the 2021-22 to 2023-24 juries, whose reports are at least two years old. Most: Mayor (10), Superintendent of Schools (4), Office of the Mayor (3).
how: Each row of the Controller’s status tables is one recommendation and one responding department. A response counts as a promise when the original answer or a later year’s answer said the recommendation "has not yet been implemented but will be implemented in the future". It is still pending when the latest answer given is that, or "requires further analysis".
limits: The 2024-25 jury’s report has only the original responses (2025), so its promises are a year old at most. On a few rows of the oldest report two respondents’ names ran together on the text layer; they are kept as printed. A recommendation may be partly done; the tables record the department’s own words, not a check. The rules let departments decline or defer for cost, legal or policy reasons.
